title: Eastern Air Lines 401
summary: Eastern Air Lines Flight 401 crashed in the Florida Everglades shortly before midnight after the autopilot inadvertently disconnected. A subtle bump of the yoke switched the autopilot from altitude hold to Control Wheel Steering mode. While the crew was focused on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, they did not notice the autopilot disconnection and the aircraft gradually lost altitude until striking the ground.
probable_cause: A subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode. The crew's focus on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light distracted them from noticing the altitude loss.

factors.evidence: A subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode, causing the aircraft to begin a descent.
Due to the focus on a malfunctioning landing gear indicator light, the pilots did not notice the autopilot being shut off.
The aircraft gradually lost altitude and the altitude warning C-chord chime was triggered but there was no indication the pilots had heard it.
Flight 401 crashed west-northwest of Miami, 18.7 mi from the end of Runway 9L.

events.text: After lowering the gear, Stockstill noticed that the landing gear indicator, a green light, had not illuminated.
Loft instructed Stockstill to put the L-1011 on autopilot and a subtle bump of the yoke caused the autopilot to switch from altitude hold mode to Control Wheel Steering mode.
The altitude warning C-chord chime located under Repo's workstation was triggered as the aircraft lost altitude.
Flight 401 crashed west-northwest of Miami, 18.7 mi from the end of Runway 9L.
